results.title: Uffizi Galleries in Florence announce €50m transformation
results.description: The Uffizi Galleries in Florence, Italy has announced a two-year, €50 million transformation, described as one of its most ambitious projects to date. Announced by Uffizi Galleries director Simone Verde , the project covers the Uffizi complex, including the Palazzo Pitti and Boboli Gardens. It includes new exhibition spaces, upgraded guest facilities, improved infrastructure, and enhancements to the institution's climate control and accessibility. “An operation of unprecedented scale and depth is underway thanks to the extraordinary commitment of the entire staff,” Verde said this week at a press conference, the Florentine reports. See on Instagram “The Uffizi will emerge even more beautiful and increasingly capable of representing one of Italy’s fundamental cultural icons.” At the Uffizi Gallery, the project includes the development of an introductory area dedicated to the history of the museum 's collections, as well as a new reception and security screening zone. Some galleries are being reinstalled and enhanced with new lighting, and accessibility is being improved with better wayfinding and signage. The Uffizi Gallery is also investing in infrastructure updates, including new air treatment and climate-control systems, as well as a planned €12 million restoration of the façades and roofs. Two-year Uffizi project underway At Palazzo Pitti, refurbishment work will be carried out, and the top floor will be converted into a new exhibition space. The palace's new entrance opened in July. Projects at the Boboli Gardens include the restoration of the amphitheatre, as well as work on the site's sculptures, pathways and greenhouses. In March, an eight-year initiative to refresh the Uffizi Gallery's historic entrance was completed. Images courtesy of the Uffizi

results.title: Diver dies while working off St Paul’s Islands
results.description: A diver has died while he was working in the waters off St Paul’s Islands, police said in a statement on Monday. Police said that the victim was a 41-year-old man who lives in Rabat. He has been named by TVM as Redeemer Grima. Officers were informed of the situation at around midday. Police said that the diver was brought ashore by the Armed Forces of Malta at the quay in Bugibba. A medical team assisted him, but he was certified dead a short time later. Magistrate Monica Borg Galea is leading an inquiry while investigations by the police and the Occupational Health and Safety Authority are also ongoing.

results.title: Tom Hiddleston on his Pompeii docu-series: Compresses timeline of 2000 years, brings remarkable story
results.description: Los Angeles, Aug 10 (IANS) British actor Tom Hiddleston, who has hosted the docu-series ‘Pompeii: Out of Time with Tom Hiddleston’, has spoken about his fascination with the historical ruins of Pompeii. He said that for him visiting Pompeii was about feeling the distance of the 2,000 years between now and then getting compressed. In the docu-series, the actor, guided by a team of archaeologists, historians, geologists and disaster experts, uncovers remarkable evidence and the stories of real people that challenge long-held assumptions about Pompeii and its final hours, not least revealing that many of those caught up in the disaster had the chance to survive. Talking about the same, Tom Hiddleston said, "The ancient world has compelled my imagination and curiosity for as long as I can remember, I've been fascinated by it all my life. Classical Antiquity is the foundation and cornerstone of Western and European culture. To visit Pompeii is to feel the distance of the 2,000 years between now and then compress. The past becomes the present; the past feels so close. Tangible, honest and real. Our relationship with the past is alive, studying who we were in order to understand who we are. Pompeii is a gateway for that conversation. It's a privilege to host this visually immersive and dynamic series”. The series blends scripted drama and investigative documentary, and transports audiences to ancient Rome in the hours before and during the eruption of Mount Vesuvius. He further mentioned, “Pompeii is often remembered for how its story ended. But by looking closer, we can uncover the details of people's lives, the choices they made, and the moments that came before the city was buried. To revisit the final hours of those ordinary people, caught in an extraordinary moment, and to help bring these remarkable human stories back into the light, is a genuine honor”. In 79 AD, Mount Vesuvius violently erupted, burying Pompeii in volcanic ash. This rapid burial froze the city in time, uniquely preserving its buildings, art and the people. ‘Pompeii: Out of Time with Tom Hiddleston’ is produced by Plimsoll Productions. Tom Barbor-Might serves as showrunner and director; Jessica Ruston and Mark Ravenhill are writers with additional writing by Kevin R. Wright and Tom Barbor-Might; and Grant Mansfield, Kevin R. Wright, Helen Flint and Alan Eyres are executive producers. The docu-series is available on National Geographic Channel and JioHotstar. --IANS aa/

results.title: Shreya Kalra says she had made peace with rumours of Shivangi Joshi being the winner on ‘Lock Upp 2’
results.description: Mumbai, Aug 10 (IANS) Shreya Kalra, who won the 2nd season of the streaming captive reality show ‘Lock Upp’, has said that she had accepted her fate of not being the winner until the news was broken to her. She said that she heard the rumours about Shivangi Joshi being crowned the winner, and shared that even Google threw up results of Shivangi being the winner. So when she heard that she had won the show, she was left shell-shocked. She told the media, “I didn’t feel that I would win the show because we have seen reality shows, and we know that a certain bias creeps in for the people who are famous while deciding the winner. The makers do it so that they could pitch it to bigger actors in the subsequent season. I was convinced that whatever I had, I gave to the show. Even if I hadn’t won the show, I won in life. I had said the same thing in my speech that the friends I made along the way in the show, the way fans supported me, I was happy in that moment”. “I heard about the rumours about Shivangi Joshi being the winner, even Google had reported the same. I had accepted it. But when I got to know that I’m the winner of the show, I was shocked”, she added. Shreya walked away with the coveted trophy and a whopping Rs 1 crore cash prize. Shivangi Joshi finished as the first runner-up, while the other finalists were Ram Kapoor, Shilpa Shinde and Yogesh Rawat. Ahead of the finale, Varun Yadav and Akanksha Chamola were eliminated from the competition. Akanksha was evicted after Yogesh, Shreya and Varun unanimously voted her out when host Riteish Deshmukh asked them to take a collective decision. --IANS aa/

results.title: Customs duty on gold, silver, platinum tops Rs 10,460 crore since duty hike
results.description: New Delhi, Aug 10 (IANS) The government has collected Rs 10,463 crore in customs duty from imports of gold, silver and platinum between May 13 and August 2 following the increase in import duties on the precious metals, Parliament was informed on Monday. In a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha, Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary said customs duty collections during the period stood at Rs 10,040 crore on gold, Rs 328 crore on silver and Rs 95 crore on platinum. The combined customs duty collection from the three precious metals thus amounted to Rs 10,463 crore during the period. With effect from May 13, the government had increased the import duty on gold and silver to 15 per cent from 6 per cent, while the duty on platinum was raised to 15.4 per cent from 6.4 per cent. Moreover, consequential changes were also made to duties on related items, including gold and silver dore, coins and findings. Chaudhary said the government had taken the decision to curb discretionary imports and prioritise foreign exchange for essential imports such as crude oil, fertilisers, industrial raw materials and capital goods. The duty hike came against the backdrop of rising global uncertainties, including the conflict in West Asia and the effective blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, which had pushed up prices of crude oil as well as food and fertiliser imports. The minister also informed the House that enforcement agencies seized 161 kg of smuggled gold and arrested 116 persons between May 13 and June 30. India is the world's second-largest consumer of gold after China with imports largely driven by demand from the jewellery sector. Gold imports account for a significant outflow of foreign exchange and are closely monitored by policymakers from a balance-of-payments perspective. --IANS ag/
